## Introduction

This vignette demonstrates how to reproduce and analyze occurrence data for **Glowworms** in Australia, using data from the [Atlas of Living Australia (ALA)](https://www.ala.org.au/). You'll learn how to download, clean, enrich, and visualize data with practical, reproducible R functions.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Load Required Packages and Utilities

All required functions are organized in `vignette-utils.R`. You can import them using:

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#source(here::here("inst/vignette-helpers/vignette-utils.R"))
utils_path <- system.file("vignette-helpers", "vignette-utils.R", package = "ecotourism")
if (file.exists(utils_path)) {
  source(utils_path, encoding = "UTF-8")
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is the glimps of your data :

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ecotourism)
data("glowworms")
glowworms |> glimpse()
```

## Visualization

### Spatial Distribution Map

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, eval=FALSE}
glowworms |> plot_map1(color_by = scientificName)
```

### Occurrence by State (Updated)

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, eval=FALSE}
glowworms |> count(sci_name, obs_state) 
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Weekly, Monthly, and Yearly Trends

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, eval=FALSE}
glowworms |> plot_bar_week()
glowworms |> plot_bar_week_100()
glowworms |> plot_bar_month()
glowworms |> plot_bar_year()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Monthly and Seasonal Pattern Analysis

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4, eval=FALSE}
plot_monthly_occurrences_by_state(organism_name)
plot_weekly_occurrences_by_state(organism_name)
plot_seasonal_occurrence_polar(organism_name)
plot_monthly_occurrence_map(organism_name)
plot_monthly_occurrence_map_by_state(organism_name)
plot_monthly_distribution_map(organism_name)
```

## Appendix

All helper functions used here are defined in:\
`vignettes/vignette-utils.R`

Work with Tourism dataset:

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# make full tourism dataset
data("tourism_region")
data("tourism_quarterly")

tourism <- tourism_quarterly |>
  dplyr::left_join(tourism_region, by = "region_id") |> 
  dplyr::left_join(ecotourism::weather_stations, by = "ws_id")
```

```{r}
# load top station for organism
data("top_stations")

top_stations_manta_rays <- top_stations |> filter(organism == "manta_rays")
```

No we can find related tourism spots

```{r}
tourism |> filter(ws_id %in% top_stations_manta_rays$ws_id)
```

If you want to match quarter data use this code:

```{r}

# 1. Aggregate manta observations to quarter
manta_quarter <- manta_rays %>%
  mutate(quarter = lubridate::floor_date(date, "quarter")) %>%
  count(quarter, name = "manta_sightings")

# 2. Make sure tourism$quarter is also floor_date
tourism_clean <- tourism %>%
  mutate(quarter = lubridate::floor_date(quarter, "quarter"))

# 3. Left join: keep all manta quarters, match tourism by quarter
manta_tourism <- manta_quarter %>%
  left_join(tourism_clean, by = "quarter")
```
